first.rationale: Two of the three named declines (activation -6%, onboarding completion -4%) are internal funnel problems, and two independent inherited records (memory_31 signup simplification, memory_86 shortened onboarding) point at the same lever, so onboarding/signup friction is the best-supported single-slot bet for durable qualified revenue. I want the source records for memory_31 and memory_86 because both are compressed claims of 'durable lift' whose original measurement windows, segments, and definitions of activation I cannot see; memory_31 is from day 12 and may predate the current product, and if both trace to one overlapping self-serve cohort the apparent convergence is illusory. I want memory_73 verified as the strongest rival: it is the direct answer to the competitor's entry pricing, but its summary reports acquisition and revenue lift and is conspicuously silent on retention, whereas memory_57 explicitly clears retention. That asymmetry suggests retention was either unmeasured or unfavorable, and discount-acquired price-sensitive SMBs are exactly the cohort that can inflate near-term revenue while degrading long-term qualified revenue, which is the stated objective. Downstream value risk also applies to my own intended action: cutting required signup fields can raise activation counts while stripping the qualification data that routes enterprise prospects into the sales-assisted path memory_44 says converts better, so a headline activation win could quietly cost pipeline quality. I therefore intend a standard experiment, not a broad rollout, instrumented on downstream qualified-pipeline and retention metrics rather than activation alone, and I will revise toward promotional_pricing or a narrower guarded test if the archive shows the onboarding results were narrow, stale, or measured only on proximal engagement.

final.rationale:
The archive resolved the key asymmetry I suspected. memory_73's summary ('strong acquisition and revenue lift') had silently dropped the load-bearing part of exp_73: 30-day retention -12%, with the original analyst explicitly concluding the discounted cohort does not survive first renewal and that targeted discounting must NOT be generalized as a sustainable-growth strategy. Against the stated objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, promotional_pricing is therefore disqualified despite being the intuitive answer to the competitor's entry pricing; the +18% qualified revenue is a pull-forward that the retention number shows is not durable. This consolidation error should be written back so the next agent does not inherit the sanitized version.

exp_86 is the cleanest available record and the best match to the presenting symptoms: completion +13%, time-to-value -2.1 days, and 30-day retention +3%. It is the rare case where the proximal funnel metric and the durable retention metric move the same direction, so a completion win here is unlikely to be a value-degrading artifact. Onboarding completion is down 4% and activation down 6%, and shorter time-to-value plausibly feeds the activation decline too, letting one slot address both internal declines.

I am scoping the experiment to flow shortening (exp_86) rather than signup-field cutting (exp_31). exp_31 is weaker and dirtier: retention -1%, qualified revenue only +4%, confirmed on SMB and explicitly not replicated elsewhere. It also carries the downstream risk I flagged before verification, since stripping signup fields removes the qualification data that routes enterprise prospects into the sales-assisted path memory_44 credits with better pipeline quality. That risk is real but avoidable by leaving the signup form intact.

Standard experiment, not broad rollout: exp_86 reports no segment breakdown, so I cannot tell whether the +3% retention holds outside self-serve, and it is now 24 days stale against a changed competitive environment. Primary readout is qualified pipeline and renewal-cycle retention, not completion rate alone. The competitor pricing pressure remains genuinely unaddressed by this choice; that is a deliberate accepted cost, and the right follow-up is a retention-instrumented segmentation of who is actually churning to the competitor rather than matching a discount the archive says burns the cohort it acquires.
